group.passage:
Today, millions of people put on glasses every morning without giving it a second thought. For most of history, however, those whose eyesight weakened with age simply had to live with a blurry view of the world. Close work such as reading and sewing grew harder each year, and many skilled workers were forced to [[1]] their trades long before they wished to.
Some readers placed a piece of polished glass or crystal on a page to [[2]] the letters, but this trick was useful only for reading. The first true eyeglasses appeared in northern Italy in the late 1200s, yet no one can take [[3]] for inventing them, because the maker’s name was never recorded. These early glasses had no arms, so users had to hold them up by hand or [[4]] them on the bridge of the nose. Even so, they were a great help to scholars and monks, who could now go on reading and writing well into old age.
After the printing press made books far more common in the mid-1400s, the [[5]] for glasses rose sharply. Lenses for people who could not see distant objects clearly followed later. Early frames, however, were [[6]] to wear and often slid down the nose. It was not until the 1700s that side arms resting on the ears became common, so wearers no longer had any [[7]] to hold their glasses in place.
For centuries, glasses were also seen as a sign of weakness or old age, and many people were [[8]] of wearing them in public. Today, attitudes have changed completely. Glasses now come in all kinds of shapes and colors, and many people choose frames that [[9]] their personality. Some even wear glasses with plain lenses simply because they like the look, turning a medical [[10]] into a fashion accessory.

tags.topic: how eyeglasses developed from hand-held lenses into a fashion accessory

1.explanation_zh: were forced to ___ their trades 需要原形及物動詞。前一句說人們上了年紀視力變差、看東西模糊，本句又說閱讀和縫紉一年比一年難，所以許多技術工人被迫「放棄」自己的手藝；long before they wished to（遠比他們希望的早）也說明這是不得已的。
evidence: Close work such as reading and sewing grew harder each year, and many skilled workers were forced to [[1]] their trades long before they wished to.

option_notes_zh.A: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在 were forced to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 their trades。
option_notes_zh.B: credit 也可當動詞（歸功於），但 were forced to credit their trades 不通；credit 屬於第 3 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify their trades（放大他們的手藝）不通；magnify 屬於第 2 格。
option_notes_zh.D: tool（名詞，工具、用具）詞性不合：空格在 were forced to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 their trades。
option_notes_zh.F: awkward（形容詞，笨拙的、不方便的）詞性不合：空格在 were forced to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 their trades。
option_notes_zh.G: need 也可當動詞，但 were forced to need their trades 不通；need 屬於第 7 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit their trades（適合他們的手藝）語意不通，也和「視力變差、被迫」的因果不合；suit 屬於第 9 格。
option_notes_zh.I: demand 也可當動詞（要求），但 were forced to demand their trades 不通；demand 屬於第 5 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.J: balance their trades（平衡他們的手藝）不通；balance 屬於第 4 格。

1.strategy_zh: to 後面要原形動詞；從「視力變差、工作越來越難」推出工人被迫「放棄」手藝。
hints: were forced to ___ their trades：to 後面要原形動詞。
視力越來越差、閱讀和縫紉越來越難，工人只好怎麼做？
give up＝放棄。

2.explanation_zh: to ___ the letters 是表目的的不定詞，需要原形及物動詞。把磨亮的玻璃或水晶放在書頁上，目的是「放大」字母，讓視力不好的人看得清楚；but this trick was useful only for reading 也說明這個方法只能用在閱讀。
evidence: Some readers placed a piece of polished glass or crystal on a page to [[2]] the letters, but this trick was useful only for reading.

option_notes_zh.A: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在表目的的不定詞 to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 the letters。
option_notes_zh.B: credit 也可當動詞，但 credit the letters 不通；credit 屬於第 3 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.D: tool（名詞，工具、用具）詞性不合：空格在表目的的不定詞 to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 the letters。
option_notes_zh.E: give up the letters（放棄字母）和「放在書頁上幫助閱讀」的目的相反；give up 屬於第 1 格。
option_notes_zh.F: awkward（形容詞，笨拙的、不方便的）詞性不合：空格在表目的的不定詞 to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 the letters。
option_notes_zh.G: need 也可當動詞，但 need the letters（需要字母）不合「放玻璃」的目的；need 屬於第 7 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit the letters（適合字母）不通；suit 屬於第 9 格。
option_notes_zh.I: demand 也可當動詞，但 demand the letters（要求字母）不通；demand 屬於第 5 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.J: balance the letters（使字母平衡）不通；balance 屬於第 4 格。

2.strategy_zh: to＋原形動詞表示目的；把玻璃放在書頁上，是為了讓字「變大」。
hints: to ___ the letters：to 後面要原形動詞。
把磨亮的玻璃放在書頁上，對字母有什麼作用？
答案的意思是「放大」。

3.explanation_zh: take ___ for 需要名詞；take credit for（因……而居功、把……歸功於自己）是固定說法。because the maker’s name was never recorded（製作者的名字從未被記錄）說明為什麼沒有人能「居功」。
evidence: The first true eyeglasses appeared in northern Italy in the late 1200s, yet no one can take [[3]] for inventing them, because the maker’s name was never recorded.

option_notes_zh.A: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在 take 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 take 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.D: take tool for inventing them 不通；tool 屬於第 10 格。
option_notes_zh.E: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 take 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.F: awkward（形容詞，笨拙的、不方便的）詞性不合：空格在 take 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.G: take need for 不通；need 屬於第 7 格。
option_notes_zh.H: suit 也可當名詞（西裝），但 take suit for inventing them 不通；suit 屬於第 9 格的動詞。
option_notes_zh.I: take demand for 不是英文說法；demand 屬於第 5 格 the demand for glasses。
option_notes_zh.J: balance 也可當名詞（平衡），但 take balance for inventing them 不通；balance 屬於第 4 格的動詞。

3.strategy_zh: 看到 take ___ for，想到固定說法 take credit for；because 子句說明沒人知道發明者是誰。
hints: take ___ for：需要名詞。
because the maker’s name was never recorded：沒人知道是誰發明的，所以沒有人能怎樣？
「居功、獲得讚揚」英文說 take ___ for。

4.explanation_zh: had to hold them … or ___ them 中，空格和 hold 由 or 連接，需要原形及物動詞。早期眼鏡 had no arms（沒有鏡腳），所以只能用手拿著，或把它們「放穩」在鼻樑上。
evidence: These early glasses had no arms, so users had to hold them up by hand or [[4]] them on the bridge of the nose.

option_notes_zh.A: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格和 hold 由 or 連接，在 had to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 them。
option_notes_zh.B: credit 也可當動詞，但 credit them on the bridge of the nose 不通；credit 屬於第 3 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify them on the bridge of the nose（在鼻樑上放大它們）不通；magnify 屬於第 2 格。
option_notes_zh.D: tool（名詞，工具、用具）詞性不合：空格和 hold 由 or 連接，在 had to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 them。
option_notes_zh.E: give up them 語序不對（應為 give them up），意思也和「戴眼鏡」相反；give up 屬於第 1 格。
option_notes_zh.F: awkward（形容詞，笨拙的、不方便的）詞性不合：空格和 hold 由 or 連接，在 had to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 them。
option_notes_zh.G: need 也可當動詞，但 need them on the bridge of the nose 不是和 hold 並列的「動作」；need 屬於第 7 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit them on the bridge of the nose 不通；suit 屬於第 9 格。
option_notes_zh.I: demand 也可當動詞，但 demand them on the bridge of the nose 不通；demand 屬於第 5 格的名詞。

4.strategy_zh: or 連接兩個原形動詞；沒有鏡腳的眼鏡，只能用手拿，或放穩在鼻樑上。
hints: hold them … or ___ them：和 hold 並列，需要原形動詞。
眼鏡 had no arms：不用手拿的話，要怎麼讓它留在鼻子上？
答案的意思是「使平衡、放穩」。

5.explanation_zh: the ___ for glasses rose sharply 需要名詞當主詞；demand for（對……的需求）是固定搭配。印刷術讓書本大量普及，讀書的人變多，對眼鏡的「需求」也急遽上升。need 只看本句也說得通（the need for glasses），但第 7 格 no longer had any ___ to hold … 只能填 need（demand 不能接 to hold），所以 need 要留給第 7 格。
evidence: After the printing press made books far more common in the mid-1400s, the [[5]] for glasses rose sharply.

option_notes_zh.A: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在 the 之後、for glasses 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.B: the credit for glasses rose（眼鏡的功勞上升）不通；credit 屬於第 3 格。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 the 之後、for glasses 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.D: the tool for glasses rose 不通；tool 屬於第 10 格。
option_notes_zh.E: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 the 之後、for glasses 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.F: awkward（形容詞，笨拙的、不方便的）詞性不合：空格在 the 之後、for glasses 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.G: need 是名詞，the need for glasses rose 只看本句可通，但第 7 格 had any ___ to hold … 只能填 need；本句講書本普及後買眼鏡的人變多，是市場上的「需求」。
option_notes_zh.H: suit 當名詞是「西裝」，the suit for glasses rose 不通；suit 屬於第 9 格。
option_notes_zh.J: balance 當名詞是「平衡」，the balance for glasses rose sharply 不通；balance 屬於第 4 格。

5.strategy_zh: 冠詞與 for 之間要名詞；由「書本普及」推出眼鏡的需求增加，並用第 7 格的 to 不定詞把 need 留給它。
hints: the ___ for glasses：需要名詞，當句子主詞。
印刷術讓書本變多，讀書的人增加，對眼鏡的什麼上升了？
比較 demand 和 need：哪一個還能放進第 7 格 had any ___ to hold …？

6.explanation_zh: were ___ to wear 需要形容詞（形容詞＋to V）。and often slid down the nose（而且常從鼻子上滑下來）說明早期鏡框戴起來「不方便」；下一句的鏡腳正是為了解決這個問題。ashamed 雖是形容詞，但主詞是 frames（鏡框），鏡框不會感到羞愧。
evidence: Early frames, however, were [[6]] to wear and often slid down the nose.

option_notes_zh.A: ashamed 是形容詞，但主詞是 frames（鏡框），物品不會「感到羞愧」；ashamed 屬於第 8 格 were ashamed of。
option_notes_zh.B: credit（名詞，功勞、讚揚；take credit for＝把……歸功於自己）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.D: tool（名詞，工具、用具）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.E: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.G: need（名詞，需要、必要）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit（動詞，適合（也可當名詞「西裝」））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.I: demand（名詞，需求（也可當動詞「要求」））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.J: balance（動詞，使平衡、放穩（也可當名詞「平衡」））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。

6.strategy_zh: 形容詞＋to V；用 often slid down the nose 判斷鏡框戴起來「不方便」，再用主詞是物品排除 ashamed。
hints: were ___ to wear：需要形容詞。
often slid down the nose：這樣的鏡框戴起來感覺如何？
答案的意思是「不方便的、笨拙的」。

7.explanation_zh: no longer had any ___ to hold … 需要名詞；have no need to V（沒有必要做……）是常用說法。鏡腳架在耳朵上之後，配戴者就「不必再」用手扶著眼鏡。demand 不能接不定詞 to hold 表示「必要」。
evidence: It was not until the 1700s that side arms resting on the ears became common, so wearers no longer had any [[7]] to hold their glasses in place.

option_notes_zh.A: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在 had any 之後、to hold 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.B: had any credit to hold their glasses 不通；credit 屬於第 3 格。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 had any 之後、to hold 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.D: had any tool to hold their glasses in place 文法可通，但前面說鏡腳已經架在耳朵上，重點是「不必再用手扶」，不是「有沒有工具」；tool 屬於第 10 格。
option_notes_zh.E: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 had any 之後、to hold 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.F: awkward（形容詞，笨拙的、不方便的）詞性不合：空格在 had any 之後、to hold 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit 當名詞是「西裝」，had any suit to hold their glasses 不通；suit 屬於第 9 格。
option_notes_zh.I: demand 是名詞，但 have any demand to hold … 不是英文說法；demand 要用在第 5 格 the demand for glasses。
option_notes_zh.J: balance 當名詞是「平衡」，had any balance to hold their glasses 不通；balance 屬於第 4 格。

7.strategy_zh: have no ___ to V 要名詞；鏡腳讓眼鏡固定，所以「不必再」用手扶。
hints: had any ___ to hold：需要名詞，後面接不定詞。
有了架在耳朵上的鏡腳，配戴者還「必須」用手扶眼鏡嗎？
have no ___ to V＝沒有必要做某事。

8.explanation_zh: were ___ of wearing them 需要能接 of 的形容詞；be ashamed of（以……為恥）是固定搭配。眼鏡被視為 a sign of weakness or old age（軟弱或衰老的象徵），所以很多人「羞於」在公開場合戴。awkward 不接 of。
evidence: For centuries, glasses were also seen as a sign of weakness or old age, and many people were [[8]] of wearing them in public.

option_notes_zh.B: credit（名詞，功勞、讚揚；take credit for＝把……歸功於自己）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.D: tool（名詞，工具、用具）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.E: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.F: awkward 是形容詞，但不和 of 搭配（awkward of wearing 不通）；awkward 屬於第 6 格 awkward to wear。
option_notes_zh.G: need（名詞，需要、必要）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit（動詞，適合（也可當名詞「西裝」））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.I: demand（名詞，需求（也可當動詞「要求」））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.J: balance（動詞，使平衡、放穩（也可當名詞「平衡」））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。

8.strategy_zh: 看介系詞 of 決定形容詞：be ashamed of；再用「軟弱、衰老的象徵」確認是羞恥的感受。
hints: were ___ of：需要能接 of 的形容詞。
眼鏡被當成軟弱、衰老的象徵，戴眼鏡的人會有什麼感受？
be ___ of＝以……為恥。

9.explanation_zh: frames that ___ their personality 中，that 代替複數的 frames，空格要用現在式的及物動詞（複數主詞用原形）。suit 當動詞是「適合」：人們挑選「適合」自己個性的鏡框，呼應前面 all kinds of shapes and colors（各式各樣的造型和顏色）。
evidence: Glasses now come in all kinds of shapes and colors, and many people choose frames that [[9]] their personality.

option_notes_zh.A: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在關係代名詞 that（先行詞 frames）之後，需要現在式的及物動詞（複數主詞用原形），受詞是 their personality。
option_notes_zh.B: credit 也可當動詞，但 frames that credit their personality 不通；credit 屬於第 3 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify their personality（放大個性）不是自然說法；magnify 屬於第 2 格。
option_notes_zh.D: tool（名詞，工具、用具）詞性不合：空格在關係代名詞 that（先行詞 frames）之後，需要現在式的及物動詞（複數主詞用原形），受詞是 their personality。
option_notes_zh.E: give up their personality（放棄個性）和「挑選喜歡的鏡框」相反；give up 屬於第 1 格。
option_notes_zh.F: awkward（形容詞，笨拙的、不方便的）詞性不合：空格在關係代名詞 that（先行詞 frames）之後，需要現在式的及物動詞（複數主詞用原形），受詞是 their personality。
option_notes_zh.G: need 也可當動詞，但 frames that need their personality 不通；need 屬於第 7 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.I: demand 也可當動詞，但 frames that demand their personality 不通；demand 屬於第 5 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.J: balance their personality（平衡他們的個性）不合「挑選鏡框」的語境；balance 屬於第 4 格。

9.strategy_zh: that 指複數的 frames，空格要現在式動詞；選鏡框的標準是「適合」自己。
hints: frames that ___ their personality：that 指 frames，空格要用現在式的動詞。
眼鏡有各種造型和顏色，人們會挑什麼樣的鏡框？
suit 除了「西裝」，當動詞是「適合」。

10.explanation_zh: a medical ___ 需要名詞。turn A into B（把 A 變成 B）：眼鏡本來是矯正視力的「醫療用具」，現在連視力正常的人也戴平光眼鏡，把它變成時尚配件。tool 是全文 glasses、eyeglasses、frames 這個東西的另一種說法（詞彙聯結）。
evidence: Some even wear glasses with plain lenses simply because they like the look, turning a medical [[10]] into a fashion accessory.

option_notes_zh.A: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在 a medical 之後，需要單數名詞。
option_notes_zh.B: a medical credit 不通；credit 屬於第 3 格。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 a medical 之後，需要單數名詞。
option_notes_zh.E: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 a medical 之後，需要單數名詞。
option_notes_zh.F: awkward（形容詞，笨拙的、不方便的）詞性不合：空格在 a medical 之後，需要單數名詞。
option_notes_zh.G: need 是名詞，但 turning a medical need into a fashion accessory（把醫療需求變成時尚配件）不合，accessory 是物品，「需求」不能變成配件；need 屬於第 7 格。

translation_zh.text:
今天，數百萬人每天早上戴上眼鏡，連想都不用想。然而在歷史上大部分時間裡，視力隨著年紀退化的人只能忍受一個模糊的世界。閱讀和縫紉這類近距離的工作一年比一年困難，許多技術工人遠比自己希望的更早就被迫放棄手藝。
有些讀者會在書頁上放一片磨亮的玻璃或水晶來放大字母，但這個方法只對閱讀有用。真正的眼鏡在十三世紀末出現在義大利北部，但沒有人能說是自己的功勞，因為製作者的名字從未被記錄下來。這些早期的眼鏡沒有鏡腳，使用者必須用手拿著，或把它們放穩在鼻樑上。即使如此，眼鏡對學者和修士仍是一大幫助，他們從此到了老年也能繼續讀書寫字。
十五世紀中葉印刷術讓書本普及之後，對眼鏡的需求急遽上升。後來又出現了給看不清楚遠處物體的人使用的鏡片。不過，早期的鏡框戴起來很不方便，常常從鼻子上滑下來。直到十八世紀，架在耳朵上的鏡腳才變得普遍，配戴者從此不必再用手扶著眼鏡。
幾百年來，眼鏡也被視為軟弱或衰老的象徵，許多人都羞於在公開場合戴眼鏡。如今，人們的看法已完全改變。眼鏡有各式各樣的造型和顏色，許多人會挑選適合自己個性的鏡框。有些人甚至只因為喜歡那種造型就戴上平光眼鏡，把一種醫療用具變成了時尚配件。

evidence: Close work such as reading and sewing grew harder each year, and many skilled workers were forced to [[1]] their trades long before they wished to.
1.explanation_zh: forced to 後接原形動詞，受詞 their trades；視力衰退被迫「放棄」本行工作，give up 最合。

evidence: Some readers placed a piece of polished glass or crystal on a page to [[2]] the letters, but this trick was useful only for reading.
2.explanation_zh: 把磨亮的玻璃放在書頁上是為了「放大」字母，magnify 為及物動詞。

evidence: The first true eyeglasses appeared in northern Italy in the late 1200s, yet no one can take [[3]] for inventing them, because the maker’s name was never recorded.
3.explanation_zh: take credit for 為固定搭配「因…而獲得功勞」，下文說發明者姓名沒有記錄。

evidence: These early glasses had no arms, so users had to hold them up by hand or [[4]] them on the bridge of the nose.
4.explanation_zh: 早期眼鏡沒有鏡腳，只能用手拿著或把它「平衡擺放」在鼻樑上，balance 與 hold up 並列為原形動詞。

evidence: After the printing press made books far more common in the mid-1400s, the [[5]] for glasses rose sharply.
5.explanation_zh: 印刷術使書變多，眼鏡的「需求」大增；the demand for ... rose sharply 為常見搭配。need 單看此句勉強可通，但 need 必須用在第 7 格。

evidence: Early frames, however, were [[6]] to wear and often slid down the nose.
6.explanation_zh: 主詞是 frames，be 動詞後接形容詞；鏡框會往下滑，戴起來「不舒服、不順手」，awkward 合理（ashamed 主詞須為人）。

evidence: It was not until the 1700s that side arms resting on the ears became common, so wearers no longer had any [[7]] to hold their glasses in place.
7.explanation_zh: no longer had any need to + V 表示「不再需要」；有了鏡腳就不必用手扶眼鏡。

evidence: For centuries, glasses were also seen as a sign of weakness or old age, and many people were [[8]] of wearing them in public.
8.explanation_zh: be ashamed of V-ing 為固定用法；眼鏡被視為軟弱或老的象徵，所以人們「羞於」在公開場合戴。

evidence: Glasses now come in all kinds of shapes and colors, and many people choose frames that [[9]] their personality.
9.explanation_zh: 關係子句中需及物動詞，主詞 frames 為複數故用原形；選擇「適合」自己個性的鏡框，suit 合理。

evidence: Some even wear glasses with plain lenses simply because they like the look, turning a medical [[10]] into a fashion accessory.
10.explanation_zh: a medical 後接名詞，與 fashion accessory 對照：把一種醫療「工具」變成時尚配件。

evidence: many skilled workers were forced to [[1]] their trades long before they wished to.
1.explanation_zh: 視力變差、近距離工作越來越難，工匠被迫「放棄」自己的行業，give up their trades 最合語意與文法。

evidence: Some readers placed a piece of polished glass or crystal on a page to [[2]] the letters
2.explanation_zh: 把拋光的玻璃放在書頁上是為了把字「放大」，magnify the letters。

evidence: no one can take [[3]] for inventing them, because the maker’s name was never recorded.
3.explanation_zh: take credit for 是固定搭配（居功），呼應發明者名字沒有留下。

evidence: so users had to hold them up by hand or [[4]] them on the bridge of the nose.
4.explanation_zh: 早期眼鏡沒有鏡腳，只能用手拿或把它「平衡」架在鼻樑上，balance them on the bridge of the nose。

evidence: After the printing press made books far more common in the mid-1400s, the [[5]] for glasses rose sharply.
5.explanation_zh: 印刷術讓書變多，眼鏡的「需求」大增，the demand for glasses rose 最自然；need 句內也說得通，但 need 在第 7 格更不可替代。

evidence: Early frames, however, were [[6]] to wear and often slid down the nose.
6.explanation_zh: 早期鏡框常滑下鼻子，所以戴起來「不舒服、笨拙」，awkward to wear。

evidence: so wearers no longer had any [[7]] to hold their glasses in place.
7.explanation_zh: 鏡腳架在耳朵上後，配戴者不再「需要」用手扶住眼鏡，no longer had any need to hold。

evidence: many people were [[8]] of wearing them in public.
8.explanation_zh: 眼鏡被視為虛弱或老態的象徵，人們「以戴眼鏡為恥」，ashamed of wearing；介系詞 of 也吻合。

evidence: many people choose frames that [[9]] their personality.
9.explanation_zh: 選擇「適合」自己個性的鏡框，frames that suit their personality。

evidence: turning a medical [[10]] into a fashion accessory.
10.explanation_zh: 眼鏡原本是醫療「工具」，現在變成時尚配件，medical tool 與 fashion accessory 對比；medical need 文法上勉強可行但語意不及 tool。
